ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $O$. If $\angle AOB = 40^\circ$ and $BC \parallel OA$, then what is the measure of $\angle ADC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because \angle AOB=40^\circ$, and OA=OB,\\
$\therefore \angle ABO=70^\circ$,\\
$\because BC\parallel OA$,\\
$\therefore \angle OBC=\angle AOB=40^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ABC=110^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle ADC=180^\circ-110^\circ=\boxed{70^\circ}$.

The radii OA and OB are drawn in the figure, and the chord BC is located above the circle. The problem statement gives BC ∥ OA, and gives ∠AOB = 40°. Reasoning: Because OA and OB are both radii of circle O, OA = OB, and triangle AOB is an isosceles triangle. It is known that ∠AOB = 40°, so the base angle ∠ABO = (180° - 40°) / 2 = 70°. Also because BC ∥ OA, the angle formed by OB and BC is equal to the angle formed by OB and OA, that is, ∠OBC = ∠AOB = 40°. Therefore ∠ABC = ∠ABO + ∠OBC = 70° + 40° = 110°. Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, so ∠ADC = 180° - ∠ABC = 180° - 110° = 70°.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: A, B, C, D lie on circle O; OA and OB are drawn as radii, and BC is a chord drawn parallel to OA. From the text, use ∠AOB = 40° and BC ∥ OA. Since OA = OB, triangle AOB is isosceles, so ∠ABO = (180° − 40°)/2 = 70°. Because BC is parallel to OA, the angle between OB and BC equals the angle between OB and OA, so ∠OBC = 40°. Thus ∠ABC = ∠ABO + ∠OBC = 70° + 40° = 110°. Finally, since ABCD is cyclic, opposite angles of an inscribed quadrilateral are supplementary, so ∠ADC = 180° − 110° = 70°.

图像描述：图中有一个以 O 为圆心的圆，A、B、C、D 四点都在圆周上，构成圆内接四边形 ABCD。图中画出了半径 OA 和 OB，弦 BC 位于圆的上方，题设给出 BC ∥ OA，并给出 ∠AOB = 40°。
推理：因为 OA 和 OB 都是圆 O 的半径，所以 OA = OB，三角形 AOB 是等腰三角形。已知 ∠AOB = 40°，所以底角 ∠ABO = (180° - 40°) / 2 = 70°。又因为 BC ∥ OA，所以 OB 与 BC 所成的角等于 OB 与 OA 所成的角，即 ∠OBC = ∠AOB = 40°。因此 ∠ABC = ∠ABO + ∠OBC = 70° + 40° = 110°。由于 ABCD 是圆内接四边形，对角互补，所以 ∠ADC = 180° - ∠ABC = 180° - 110° = 70°。
